title: Minimax Theory of Likelihood-Based Deep Learning for Speckle Regression
summary: Speckle noise is a multiplicative noise commonly encountered in coherent imaging modalities such as synthetic aperture radar, optical coherence tomography, and digital holography. Although deep learning methods, in practice, have achieved state-of-the-art performance for speckle denoising, their fundamental statistical limits remain largely unexplored. Unlike additive noise models, multiplicative speckle noise makes the regression function unidentifiable from the conditional mean, rendering conventional least-squares-based deep learning approaches inapplicable.
